correctness.rationale: All interior equilibria follow exactly from three environmental equilibrium equations and two payoff equations, with 0<kappa<2 verified. The Jacobian is differentiated from all five displayed equations. Exact determinant elimination gives lambda times a quartic with four positive coefficients. Its two nontrivial Routh inequalities are strictly positive and a nonnegative square, the latter vanishing precisely at equal feedback rates. At equality, factorization yields one nonzero imaginary pair and two stable eigenvalues. A simple zero tangent mode and normal-hyperbolicity theory establish local exponential point convergence in the asymmetric case; the explicit conserved log-odds value determines that point. The supplied checker independently verifies algebraic identities and 27 rational finite examples, without relying on finite tests to prove the parameter-uniform theorem.

value.rationale: The study of eco-evolutionary interaction networks motivates deciding whether fully interior coexistence trajectories converge or exhibit persistent linear oscillations. In the existing five-dimensional model, the threshold is exactly environmental response symmetry, independent of other admissible payoff coefficients and location along the interior curve. The quantified strictly positive Hurwitz determinant and exact neutral-case factor are structural and show how response heterogeneity stabilizes a balanced-mixing community network. Conservation then identifies the locally selected terminal equilibrium. This is distinct from discovering an equilibrium line alone, computing a handful of eigenvalues, or applying a textbook test without an analytically motivated all-parameter factorization.
